question: The ‘Tripitaka’ is a holy book of which religion from following ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is** Buddhism.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The three holy texts of Buddhism are known as **Tripitaka**. 
 
• The Tripitaka is regarded as the oral transmission of the **Buddha's teachings** that were preserved in writing by the Buddha's followers.
 
• The Buddha's successor,** Mahakashypa**, coordinated the reciting of these verses with the approval of other disciples.
 
• Buddhism regards the "**Tripitaka**" scriptures as its holy text.
 
• The **Three Pitakas** are:
 
 
• **Vinaya Pitaka**, which deals with order conduct.
 
• **Sutta Pitaka**, which is the largest collection of Buddha's teachings.
 
• **The Abhidhamma Pitaka**, a work on metaphysics.
 
 
 
• Many different** Buddishit Councils** are thought to have assembled these works.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zoroastrianism**

 
 
• **Zoroastrianism** is an **Iranian religion** and one of the world's earliest organised faiths, founded on the teachings of **Zoroaster**, an **Iranian**-speaking prophet.
 
• It has a **dualistic cosmology **of good and evil within the setting of a **monotheistic ontology,** as well as an **eschatology** that predicts the ultimate triumph of good over evil.
 
 **Jainism**

 
 
• **Jainism** is an **Indian religion** also referred to as the **Jain Dharma.** Through the succession of twenty-four **Tirthankaras** (supreme preachers of Dharma), **Jainism** traces its spiritual ideas and history.
 
• The beginning of the present time cycle, according to tradition, was **Rishabhadeva**, who lived millions of years ago. 

 The twenty-third **Tirthankara, Parshvanatha,** is believed to have lived in the ninth century BCE. The twenty-fourth** Tirthankara, Mahavira,** is believed to have lived around **600 BCE**.
